svg.text: v12 — Model service: the answer model in its own process, with a bounded queue
PROBLEM: the model lived in every API process (2,380 MB each) and nothing limited the line: 8 users → slowest answer 99 s.
FIX: one model service process owns the model; the API calls it over HTTP; at most 4 answers run or wait, the 5th gets 503 + Retry-After at once.
API PROCESS(ES) — app/main.py · ~1 GB each · no model
POST /answers or POST /answers/stream
{"question": "How do I cancel my subscription?"}
router.py → service.py (unchanged since v11)
token · rate limit · retrieve (embeddings + pgvector)
threshold 0.30 · build the prompt (3 sources + question)
generator.py — now an HTTP client (httpx)
generate() → POST /generate · generate_stream() → POST /generate/stream
down / timeout 120 s → GenerationUnavailable → 503
busy → GenerationBusy → 503 + Retry-After: 10
streams: status checked BEFORE the API's first line, so 503 stays a 503
Responses (unchanged, plus one new case)
200 {"answer": "Workspace owners can cancel from…", "sources": [...]}
200 NDJSON: sources → text … → done
NEW 503 {"detail": "The answer model is busy; try again shortly"}
header Retry-After: 10 (in ≤ 1.1 s, no model time spent)
503 "…try GET /documents/search?mode=semantic" when the service is down
HTTP :8001
{"messages": [...], "max_tokens": 200}
{"text": "…"} / 503 busy
MODEL SERVICE — app/model_service/ · ONE process · NEW
runs AI inference separately from the main API · uvicorn app.model_service.main:app --port 8001
main.py — enter_queue(): MODEL_MAX_QUEUE = 4
running + waiting < 4 → take a place, continue
4 already → 503 "The model is busy", Retry-After: 10
leave_queue() in "finally": after answers, streams, crashes
backpressure: tell the caller "later" instead of letting work pile up
model.py — the lock, then llama.cpp (moved from the API)
Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct q4 GGUF · temperature 0 · one answer at a time
loaded once at start (lifespan) — the only copy on the machine
log: "answer: waited 8.4 s for the model, generated in 5.7 s"
only file allowed to use llama_cpp (a test checks it)
POST /generate → {"text": "…"}
POST /generate/stream → {"text": "…"} lines, or {"error": "…"}
no model loaded → 503 · request invalid → 422
GET /health
{"status": "ok", "model_loaded": true, "in_queue": 0, "max_queue": 4}
the line of waiting answers is now visible
MEASURED LOCALLY — CPU laptop (i5-13420H, 8 GB RAM, ~400 MB free), scripts/load_test_answers.py, 3 different questions per user
8 simultaneous users (24 questions)
v11 in the API: P50 59.0 s · P95 93.0 · max 99.1 s
service, no limit: 53.9 · 93.2 · 93.4 s
queue 4, 8 users alone: 33.5 · 38.2 · 38.4 s
busy answers returned in ≤ 1.1 s · run 1's 93 s was
before the timing log existed: cause unknown
Memory (Windows private bytes)
v11: 1 API process = 2,380 MB
v12: API 981 MB + model service 1,802 MB
v11, 2 workers: not run (~4.8 GB estimated)
with 2 workers one API worker died silently at
the first 4 questions (~400 MB free); uvicorn
restarted it; 7 of 8 answered
What did NOT change
answers / min: 4–11 in every setup, 1–8 users
(one CPU, one model — no speed-up claimed)
/health P50: 21–31 ms in every setup
(llama.cpp releases the GIL — not a reason)
generation per answer: 3.4–18.7 s (logged)
longest wait: 47.9 s with 3 answers ahead
the limit bounds HOW MANY wait, not how long
NEXT LIMITATION
• Capacity is one CPU: 5–10 answers a minute; half of 8 simultaneous users are told "busy". Real capacity needs a GPU + a batching engine (v15-llm-serving).
• Repeated questions ("How do I reset my password?") cost the full 6–10 s every time → candidate v13-caching, after measuring how often questions repeat.
• The API's own /health does not check the model service; it finds out only when an answer fails.
• Three processes to run (API, worker, model service) and the laptop is at its memory limit (~400 MB free).
• Still open from before: wrong answers not detected at runtime; retrieval misses paraphrases (sources right 0.80).
